correctness.rationale: The canonical phase-difference reduction is an exact subtraction of the source three-site ODE. Trigonometric factorization identifies two regular triangular period annuli and three stationary phase configurations. For E>0 the two branches of H=E lead to an exact primitive full-period integral. Its left and right rescalings \(E^{1/3}\) yield integrable kernels 4/(sqrt(t)*sqrt(t^3+8)) and 4/(sqrt(t)*sqrt(t^3-8)), respectively, with explicit turning-point majorants; beta integration gives \(2B(1/3,1/2)\). The Hessian determinant 9/4 gives center limit \(4\pi/3\). Supplied VERIFY.py executed, checked beta identities and five E values. The finite checks are supportive, not used to infer the infinite limit.

value.rationale: A physical-time period at a natural conservative endpoint quantifies energy-resolved critical slowing not characterized by the already-known existence of a Hamiltonian or a generic periodic island. The exact coefficient combines two geometrically inequivalent turning regimes, and the polynomial \(E^{-1/3}\) law sharply contrasts with the logarithmic law of hyperbolic separatrices. This is a complete natural period invariant for the smallest nontrivial phase ring and a meaningful diagnostic for the source family, without claiming extension to larger lattices.
